findings.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go:30 — userPermDenialCacheKey concatenates action/name/parent with unescaped "_" separators (shared with userPermCacheKey's own "_" delimiter), so distinct (action,name,parent) tuples such as (action="a_b",name="c",parent="d") and (action="a",name="b_c",parent="d") collide on the same cache key, letting a denial for one resource silently apply to an unrelated one.

pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go:30 — userPermDenialCacheKey joins action, name, parent with unescaped "_" delimiters, so distinct (name,parent) pairs such as name="a_b",parent="c" and name="a",parent="b_c" (Grafana UIDs allow underscores) collide into the same cache key, letting a cached denial for one resource be served for an unrelated resource of the same user/action

pkg/services/authz/rbac.go:101 — ProvideAuthZClient now wires the in-proc authzlib client with NoopCache while newRemoteRBACClient (rbac.go:160) still uses cache.NewLocalCache, so client-side Check/List caching behavior (and its staleness window after a permission revocation) differs between local in-proc and remote/cloud deployment modes; verify this asymmetry is intentional and documented rather than an oversight

goldens.comment: The Check operation exhibits asymmetric cache trust logic: cached permission grants are trusted and returned immediately, but cached denials from the same permission cache are ignored, leading to a fresh database lookup. This allows stale cached grants to provide access to revoked resources, posing a security risk.
The test comment says the cached permissions 'allow access', but the map stores false for dashboards:uid:dash1, so checkPermission will still treat this scope as not allowed.

The cache key construction in `userPermDenialCacheKey` uses simple string concatenation with underscores, which can lead to ambiguous keys and collision risks when any component contains underscores or is empty. This could result in incorrect denial cache hits, affecting user permissions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:123 — Error from getCachedIdentityPermissions (e.g. a real DB error from GetUserIdentifiers) is treated identically to cache.ErrNotFound and silently discarded without logging, hiding DB connectivity issues behind normal cache-miss behavior

adjudication.rationale: In Service.Check, the code calls getCachedIdentityPermissions and only uses the cached path when err == nil; any non-nil error (including a real error returned from GetUserIdentifiers inside getCachedIdentityPermissions) is treated the same as cache.ErrNotFound and is not logged before falling back to getIdentityPermissions (the DB path) (service.go around the new block starting near line ~113). The same pattern exists in List: non-nil err from getCachedIdentityPermissions is treated as a cache miss with no logging (service.go List changes). This is a diff-grounded observability/error-handling concern, but it doesn’t clearly introduce incorrect behavior because the subsequent DB path will still log/return an error if the underlying problem persists.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go:30 — userPermDenialCacheKey joins action, name, parent with unescaped "_" delimiters, so distinct (name,parent) pairs such as name="a_b",parent="c" and name="a",parent="b_c" (Grafana UIDs allow underscores) collide into the same cache key, letting a cached denial for one resource be served for an unrelated resource of the same user/action

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `userPermDenialCacheKey` in `pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go` that builds a cache key by concatenating `action`, `name`, and `parent` with raw "_" delimiters: `namespace + ".perm_" + userUID + "_" + action + "_" + name + "_" + parent`. This encoding is ambiguous if any component can contain underscores, so different (name,parent) pairs can map to the same key (e.g., `name="a_b", parent="c"` vs `name="a", parent="b_c"`). Since `Service.Check` now short-circuits to deny when `permDenialCache` has an entry for that key, such collisions can cause an unrelated resource check to be denied due to a cached denial from a different resource.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac.go:101 — ProvideAuthZClient now wires the in-proc authzlib client with NoopCache while newRemoteRBACClient (rbac.go:160) still uses cache.NewLocalCache, so client-side Check/List caching behavior (and its staleness window after a permission revocation) differs between local in-proc and remote/cloud deployment modes; verify this asymmetry is intentional and documented rather than an oversight

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows an intentional-looking divergence in client caching configuration: ProvideAuthZClient now constructs an authzlib client with a NoopCache (rbac.go around the new authzlib.NewClient call), while newRemoteRBACClient still configures a real local cache via cache.NewLocalCache(...) passed to WithCacheClientOption (rbac.go where newRBACClient was inlined). This means in-proc vs remote deployments will have different client-side cache/staleness characteristics for Check/List. The diff does not prove this is incorrect, but it is a concrete, architecture/behavior asymmetry introduced/retained by the change that should be confirmed as intended and ideally documented.
